title: P5 · His record is read and he is treated
description: The EMR follows the link to Malaysia's HIE and retrieves Kamal's summary. Dr Faisal sees the insulin and the penicillin allergy before he treats him for heat exhaustion and low blood sugar. The EMR keeps a rendered copy of the summary with the record of the visit. Step 5 of the overview of key process flows.
where: Treatment bay, Hajj health facility, Mina

illustrationStyle.prompt: Warm, flat digital illustration with soft shading and clean outlines, friendly and respectful, in the style of a public-health storybook. Wide banner, aspect ratio 11:4. Bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette with clear colour accents. Faces in gentle three-quarter view with expressive, kind features. Technology shown as simple, oversized icons: a phone with a QR code, a shield with a check mark, a small speech bubble with a symbol. No readable text, no logos, no real brands, no flags with text. All people are fictional.

cast.description: Malaysian man, 61, slim, short grey hair, kind face. Batik shirt in Malaysia. In KSA, white two-piece ihram (unstitched towelling cloth, right shoulder bare when in ihram), a small waist pouch and one phone.
His wife, about 58. White modest Hajj outfit and white telekung-style hijab in KSA; pastel baju kurung and tudung in Malaysia.
Saudi emergency doctor, 40s, short beard, white coat over a thobe.

notes: Ihram (two white unstitched sheets) is for men only; women wear ordinary modest clothing, usually white, face and hands uncovered.
Keep the Kaaba and other holy sites far in the background or out of frame.
Keep medical signs text-free so generators don't invent wrong Arabic.
The picture carries no text: the step title and the caption are page text.

steps.title: His record is read and he is treated
steps.headline: The EMR retrieves Kamal's summary from Malaysia; Dr Faisal sees the insulin and the penicillin allergy before he treats him.
steps.where: Treatment bay, Hajj health facility, Mina
steps.narrative: The EMR follows the link to Malaysia's HIE and retrieves Kamal's summary. Dr Faisal sees the insulin and the penicillin allergy before he treats him for heat exhaustion and low blood sugar. The EMR keeps a rendered copy of the summary with the record of the visit. Step 5 of the overview of key process flows.

experiences.doing: Reads the summary, sees the insulin and the penicillin allergy, and treats heat exhaustion and low blood sugar.
experiences.feeling: “Insulin, and allergic to penicillin. Glad I know before I start.”
“I did not have to explain a thing.”
“They knew about his sugar straight away.”

experiences.doing: Retrieves the VHL folder and the IPS from Malaysia's HIE, verifies the IPS, and keeps a rendered copy with the visit.
Checks the request against Kamal's consent and returns the folder and the IPS.

steps.painPoint: Treating without knowing the insulin or the penicillin allergy risks a dangerous mistake.
steps.enabler: The summary is fetched from home through the link, under the consent Kamal gave, and kept as a rendered copy with the visit.
steps.policy: Does Malaysia learn that Kamal's record was opened in KSA, and by whom?

handoff.summary: Kamal is treated, and a rendered copy is kept with the visit
handoff.payload: VHL folder (List) and the IPS Bundle

gaps: The summary is in the language it was written in; nothing says how a Saudi clinician reads a summary written in Malay.

references.label: Host Country EMR: keeps a rendered copy

illustration.alt: Kamal lies recovering on a bed with a drip, Salmah beside him; Dr Faisal shows a tablet with an insulin pen, a crossed-out penicillin capsule and a heart, read from the record kept in Malaysia.
illustration.prompt: A treatment bay. Kamal lies on a bed in white ihram with an IV drip, recovering; Salmah sits beside him, relieved. Dr Faisal looks at a tablet showing three large icons: an insulin pen, a red crossed-out penicillin capsule, and a heart. A thin dotted line runs from the tablet off-frame to a small Malaysian-roofed building icon in a cloud bubble: the record is viewed from home, not copied. Dr Faisal looks confident.
